chunks: What al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir, from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Yazīd ibn Ḍamrah al-Laythī, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who will be occupied at the time of zawāl: may he perform it earlier from the beginning of the day? He said: Yes, if he knows that he will be occupied, then he may perform it earlier in the early part of the whole day.

key_terms.صَدْرِ ٱلنَّهَارِ: the early part of the day
key_terms.كُلِّهِ: all of it; here indicating the early daytime period generally
key_terms.يَشْتَغِلُ: to be occupied or preoccupied with something
key_terms.يُعَجِّلُ: to advance or perform earlier than the usual time
key_terms.ٱلزَّوَالِ: the sun’s decline from the meridian, marking the onset of noon time

ai.seo_question: Can the daytime nawafil be performed before zawāl if a person expects to be busy later?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the time of the daytime nawafil. Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام permits bringing them forward to the early part of the day for someone who knows he will be occupied at the time of zawāl.
